question.text: Which of the following expenses related to fund operations CANNOT be charged to the Category III AIF (i.e., must be borne by the Investment Manager itself)?

answer.text: Statutory audit fees of the AIF.
Investment Manager's office lease, travel expenses, and internal salary costs.
PPM audit fees and legal agreement drafting charges.

explanation.text: The Logic: Expenses directly attributable to the investment-management function — including office lease, travel, outsourced support for investment due diligence, transaction documentation for deal execution, and IM staff salaries — MUST be borne by the Investment Manager out of its management fee, and CANNOT be charged to the AIF. Expenses for external service providers (custodian, RTA, audit, PPM audit, legal drafting) are legitimate fund expenses. The Trap: Options A, B, D are all legitimate fund expenses. The trap is confusing the IM's own operational costs with fund-level expenses. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-D test the same IM-cost segregation rule. XXI-B has a parallel rule for PMs (certain PM operating costs borne by PM, not client). Manager's Pro-Tip: Draw a 'cost waterline' in your IMA: above-the-line = IM-borne (salaries, research terminals, travel); below-the-line = fund-borne (external services). Annual investor letters should reconcile management fee vs IM operating cost — this transparency builds LP trust and pre-empts SEBI inspection findings on expense pass-through abuse.
